Subject: Private VPC endpoint TLS termination — SNI anchoring + customer CA options

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security and infra teams reviewed the private deployment patterns and we have a few hard requirements for any private endpoint that will accept traffic from our VPC:

- End-to-end mutual authentication for client→edge (customer-authn) and edge→Redwood (server-authn) where Redwood can validate a customer-supplied CA.
- Option to anchor by SNI at our edge (preferred) so we present our cert chain upstream to Redwood.
- If Redwood must terminate TLS in your private runtime, we need the ability to upload a customer root CA (or provide an intermediate chain) and have predictable rotation semantics (minimum 90-day notification, ability to negotiate emergency rotation).
- OCSP/CRL handling and an SLA for stapling or acceptable failure modes.
- DNS split-horizon guidance: we operate split DNS for private FQDNs and want a clear mapping for SRV/CNAME patterns that Redwood will accept.

Can you put together a concise ops-level runbook and a short diagram we can walk through with our network team? Also please confirm what proof we need for our CA (fingerprint, public-only chain, CSR acceptance).

Attaching a quick note from our infra team with the CA fingerprint (bb-ca-fingerprint.txt). Happy to set up a call next week if helpful.

Best,
Jane
Network Security Lead
Brightbridge Systems

Jane — we'll aim to get a first draft by EOD Monday and propose a 30-min engineering sync for Wed to review.

Hi all — thanks, Evelyn and Jane. Attached: vpc-sni-anchor-runbook-v0.1.pdf and mTLS-handshake-diagram.pdf (high-level).

Executive recommendation (short):
- Primary: SNI anchoring at Brightbridge edge → Redwood private endpoint in the same VPC. Brightbridge presents their cert chain; Redwood validates based on the SNI-anchored mapping and honors the presented chain (no Redwood private CA needed). This preserves customer control of keys and rotation.

- Secondary (if anchoring infeasible): Redwood terminates TLS in private runtime using a customer-supplied CA. This requires: upload of PEM-encoded root or intermediate (public-only), a signed proof-of-possession via SHA-256 fingerprint, and a short verification window (we recommend a 36–72 hour pre-cutover test period).

Technical notes and ops checklist (from runbook):
1) DNS expectations (split-horizon):
   - Private FQDN pattern: <env>.rbw-private.<customer-domain> -> CNAME to redwood-private.<region>.rbw.internal (we accept SRV for service discovery when multi-port routing is required).
   - TTL guidance: 60s for initial cutover; standard 300s thereafter. Ensure split-horizon authoritative answers inside customer VPC.

2) SNI anchoring behavior:
   - Redwood's private listener does NOT terminate the client cert when SNI-anchored; it forwards TLS to the runtime using a TLS pass-through mode where the presented client cert is available to the runtime via the edge's L4 passthrough/KV.
   - For health checks and telemetry we validate the server side with OCSP stapling only when Redwood acts as TLS terminator. If pass-through, OCSP is customer's responsibility.

3) Customer CA upload (if Redwood terminates):
   - Acceptable formats: PEM chain (one or more certificates, base64), DER (if indicated).
   - Required proof: SHA-256 fingerprint (hex), public key modulus info for RSA, or SPKI for ECDSA. We do NOT accept private keys.
   - Rotation: submit new cert/intermediate; Redwood will perform a canary swap across a single dedicated node, wait 10 minutes, and then gradually roll. We require 90 days notice for planned rotations; emergency rotation accepted with a signed company SLO exception + 1 hour notification for critical compromises.

4) OCSP/CRL:
   - If Redwood terminates: we will attempt OCSP stapling. If stapling fails, we follow the configured policy: FAIL_OPEN (default: allow) or FAIL_CLOSED (only for customers who opt-in). Brightbridge must indicate preference.

5) Verification checklist for dry-run:
   - Provide PEM chain + fingerprint, set up split-horizon CNAME to our staging private endpoint, set TTL=60s, perform three successive requests at t=0 / t=10m / t=30m showing preserved cert chain / client cert presence, collect pcap if needed.

6) Audit/logging:
   - We will emit an assertion log per request that includes SNI value (if present), TLS version/cipher, and certificate fingerprint (public only). Logs will be available in the Redwood Console under the customer private deployment space and retained per contract.

Next steps:
- Jane: can you confirm whether Brightbridge will opt for FAIL_OPEN vs FAIL_CLOSED for stapling fallback?
- Jane: please confirm format of the fingerprint you provided (looks like SHA-256 hex) and whether you will provide an intermediate or the root only.
- Marissa/Ben: I'll attach the runbook for your review; once we align, propose Wed 14-Feb 10:00 PST for a 30m sync to validate the staging dry-run.

Thanks — attaching runbook + diagram.

—Karthik

Thanks everyone — we've reviewed the runbook and the recommended default (SNI anchoring) works best for us. A few final constraints from our side:

- CA profile: SHA-256 fingerprint, RSA keys (minimum 3072 bits; preferred RSA-4096). If ECDSA is used, P-384 curve only.
- Rotation window: planned rotations will be cadence 90 days, but we reserve the ability to request emergency rotation if a key compromise is suspected.
- OCSP policy: Brightbridge requests FAIL_CLOSED for the staging private endpoint and will evaluate for production after the dry-run.

I've re-attached the fingerprint file (bb-ca-fingerprint.txt) and included a short PEM excerpt in case it's helpful. We confirm Wed 14-Feb 10:00 PST for the sync — please send a calendar invite.
